chunks: From him, from Muhammad ibn 'Isa, from al-Dihqan, from Durust, from Ibrahim ibn 'Abd al-Hamid, from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him), who said:

A group of people came to the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) and complained to him about the rapid depletion of their food. He (peace be upon him and his family) said, 'Do you measure (precisely) or do you scoop (generously)?' They said, 'We scoop, O Messenger of Allah,' meaning the rough, unmeasured scoop. He said to them, 'Measure, for it is greater for blessing.'
ai.seo_question: Why did the Prophet advise measuring food to increase blessing?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, the Prophet (peace be upon him) corrects the people's practice of 'tahil' (scooping roughly without leveling), advising precise measurement ('kayl') as the source of increased barakah. Shia scholars, such as Al-Tusi, highlight this as a practical application of justice in trade and consumption, linking physical precision in handling provisions to spiritual abundance. This teaching underscores that meticulousness in daily transactions is not merely administrative but a means of preserving divine blessing.
